hero.caption:
The Derby Silk Mill (Derby Museum of Industry) showcases much of the city and counties rich industrial heritage. It is part of the Derwent Valley Mills World Heritage Site - the East Midlands only such heritage site.
This particular Mill is the world first Silk Mill, and thus one of the worlds most historically important buildings. 

Derby City Council recently applied for lottery funding to upgrade the museum however was rejected. This shot is currently impossible to take due to the Cathedral Green landscaping work.

images.caption: Derby Industrial Museum - grasshopper beam engine. Grasshopper beam engine of 5 horsepower with a slide valve cylinder 9" bore by 20" stroke. Built about 1850 by the Derby born engineer George Fletcher to power machinery in his London workshop. In 1863 it was moved to his new Masson works in Litchurch Lane, Derby where it worked until 1911. It was put on display at the Museum in 1975 and restored to steam in 1993/4. It usually runs on one day a month but the museum is closing for an unknown length of time at the end of March and the engine's last run for the foreseeable future may be late February.

images.caption: Derby Industrial Museum - gates. Fine gates by Robert Bakewell that used to be across the bridge crossing the tail race and barred entry to Lombe's silk mill. This position is close to the original but to one side and perpendicular. The low cover beyond is over the parts of the steam winding engine from Morton Colliery (I thought this had long since been scrapped). Beyond that the arched window is the end of the gallery housing a Rolls-Royce RB211 engine.

images.caption: Derby Industrial Museum - RB211. Rolls-Royce RB211 high-bypass ratio gas turbine (turbo-fan) of a three shaft design. Although almost bankrupting R-R during development it is now a commercial success story and powers many of the world's large aircraft. Unfortunately the museum is to close for an unspecified period at the end of March 2011.
